title: Al-Quddus, the Most Holy
hookLine: the Most Holy, pure from every flaw

cards: Musa is walking through the desert with his family, cold and lost. Far off, he sees a fire. Stay here, he tells them; maybe I can bring back a burning stick, or find someone who knows the way.
He walks toward it. And when he gets close, the Qur'an says in Surah Ta Ha, he is called by name. O Musa.
The voice tells him to do something first. Before the revelation, before the mission, before Pharaoh. One small, physical thing, because of where he's standing.

teach.b: Take off your sandals, the voice says. You are in the holy valley, Tuwa. The word for holy there is muqaddas, from the root q-d-s, the same root as today's name.
Al-Quddus: the Most Holy, the utterly pure, free from every flaw, every lack, everything unworthy. The name comes twice in the Qur'an, both times right beside yesterday's.

At the end of al-Hashr, in Pickthall's words: the Sovereign Lord, the Holy One. And at the start of al-Jumu'ah, the same pair: al-Malik al-Quddus, the King, the Holy. The root runs through places Muslims love.

teach.h: AL-QUDS, THE HOLY LAND, THE SPIRIT.
teach.b: Jerusalem is al-Quds, the holy, and an older name for it is Bayt al-Maqdis, the house of holiness. Musa told his people to enter al-ard al-muqaddasah, the holy land.
And the Qur'an speaks of ruh al-qudus, the spirit of holiness, whom commentators identify with the angel Gabriel. What does holiness mean here?
Scholars explain it as being set apart and pure: above anything the mind can imagine, and free of the flaws people find in themselves.
So in the bowing of the prayer, Muslims may say words the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ said there, which Muslim records: subbuhun quddus, glorified, holy, Lord of the angels and the Spirit.
And after the night prayer of witr, he would say three times: subhan al-Malik al-Quddus. Glory to the King, the Holy.
Notice what Musa is asked to do in the presence of the holy. Not a speech. He is asked to take something off.
Holiness asks for a little clearing.

how: Muslims glorify Allah as al-Quddus in the prayer, some saying subbuhun quddus in the bowing or prostration, and subhan al-Malik al-Quddus three times after the witr prayer, following the Prophet's practice; ritual purity and a clean place are required for prayer.

o: the one most worshipped in holy places
utterly pure, set apart from every flaw
the one who washes people clean of sin

games.q: the root of holiness — tap the pairs.

s: al-Quddus appears in the Qur'an only once
twice: al-Hashr and al-Jumu'ah, both beside al-Malik.
Jerusalem's Arabic name shares a root with al-Quddus
the Qur'an speaks of ruh al-qudus, the spirit of holiness

games.q: you're Musa. you've walked toward a fire and a voice calls your name. what are you told to do first?
games.why: take off your sandals: you are in the holy valley, Tuwa (20:12). the revelation comes after.

practice: Find one small space near you, a corner of a desk, a windowsill, a patch of floor, and clear it, wiping it if it needs it.

Then sit near it in the quiet, no phone, no noise, shoes off if you like, as Musa was told, and notice how a cleared space changes the air around it. If you pray, you can say softly, subhan al-Malik al-Quddus.

wordCard.voice: Al-Quddus. The Most Holy, pure and set apart from every flaw; the root of al-Quds and of the holy valley where Musa was told to take off his sandals. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Most Holy, the utterly pure, from q-d-s.

carryVoice: Your line: the pure one. No flaw, no lack, nothing unworthy at all. See you tomorrow.
